newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ALPINE SKIING-RIEGLER GETS SECOND SLALOM WIN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-RIEGLER GETS SECOND SLALOM WIN.

text.p: New Zealand's Claudia Riegler collected her second World Cup slalom win of the season on Saturday to keep her 100 percent record in the discipline intact.

Riegler, who also won the first slalom of the season a month ago in Park City, clocked the second best time in both trips down the icy Nationale course, finishing with a two-run combined time of one minute 29.83 seconds.
It was the Austrian-born Riegler's third career World Cup win.
Sweden's world champion Pernilla Wiberg held a delicate advantage of 23 hundredths of a second over Riegler after the first leg.
But she was unable to protect her lead and had to settle for second for the second consecutive slalom race with a time of 1:30.50.
Patricia Chauvet of France was third in 1:30.54 followed by teammate Leila Piccard, who had the fastest second run of 44.62 seconds to move from 13th after the first leg to fourth.
German Katja Seizinger, the overall World Cup leader, was suffering from the flu did not race.
